title.en: The Jomsvikings' Founding: Palnatoki's Brotherhood and Its Oath
title.zh: 約姆斯維京的創立：帕爾納托基的兄弟會與其誓言

region.en: Jomsborg on the Baltic (the fortress; symbolic pin at Wolin, Poland)
region.zh: 波羅的海約姆斯堡（象徵性定位於波蘭沃林）

texts.period: Jomsvikinga saga 13th c. (older material); the Jomsviking-lay of Bishop Bjarni (c. 1200); the Battle of Hjorungavag c. 986

source.work: Jomsvikinga saga; the Jomsviking-lay; English: Lee M. Hollander, The Saga of the Jomsvikings, 1955 (paraphrased)

texts.license: Public domain (older editions); Hollander 1955 passages are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: The warrior-brotherhood's charter: Palnatoki of Fyn founds the fortress Jomsborg on the Wendish coast and gives the brotherhood its law - no man under eighteen, no kin-feuds inside the walls, no flight from an even fight, no word of fear, all spoils in common; the entry-trials at the founding feast, and the fall at Hjorungavag: the fleet beaten by the jarls' weather-magic, the oath-bound brothers dying on the beach in order. The record is the warrior-constitution file.
summary.zh: 戰士兄弟會的憲章：菲英島的帕爾納托基在文德海岸築起約姆斯堡，並為兄弟會立法——未滿十八歲者不得入會，牆內不得涉血仇，勢均之戰不得退逃，不得言懼，戰利品共享；創立宴上的入會考驗，以及赫約倫加瓦格之敗：艦隊被伯爵們的天氣魔法擊潰，受誓約束縛的兄弟們依序在海灘上受刑而死。此記錄是戰士憲法檔案。

texts.canonical_translation: Lee M. Hollander, The Saga of the Jomsvikings, Austin 1955 (paraphrased); Jomsvikinga saga ed. Islenzk Fornrit IX

narrative.en:
The warrior-constitution file holds the Jomsvikings' founding and fall. The founding: Palnatoki's fortress (the Baltic stronghold raised with captured labor on the Wendish shore - the brotherhood's base, its name Jomsborg), and the law: the constitution-clauses - no man under eighteen; no kin-feuds within the walls; no flight from an even fight; no word of fear however wounded; all spoils in common - the oath-register: a band governed by contract, the corpus's clearest institution-portrait of a professional warrior-state.

The recruitment-feats: the entry-trials at the founding feast (Vagn Akason's boy-oath - the twelve-year-old vowing the exploit that wins his seat), and the brotherhood's roster of champions (Bui the Broad, Sigvaldi the wily, Thorkel the Tall). And the fall at Hjorungavag: the fleet sailing against the jarls of Hladir beaten by weather-magic (the jarls' sorcery binding the winds against the raid), the battle on the beach, and the executions in order (the brothers dying by lot in their armor - the oath's last clause kept: no flight from an even fight, the execution-scene as the constitution's final exam).

The record's cultural functions are the warrior-constitution doctrine (the band as a contract-state: law before blood - a professional brotherhood's charter) and the oath-kept-in-death doctrine: the fall's executions are the constitution's proof. In the atlas, the record anchors the warrior-brotherhood family: each a tradition's professional fighting order; the Norse one is distinctive in the law's precedence over kinship.

For the database, this node complements the founding-records: here the brotherhood's charter-file.

The record's reception completes the file: the Jomsvikings' afterlife in Danish and Scandinavian memory (the brotherhood as the north's professional-warrior ideal, its code quoted by later militia-traditions), and the fortress's archaeology (the Wolin ring-fortress candidate, the harbor-works of the Baltic site) - the charter-document's material residue. And the saga's literary craft completes it: the execution-scene's order (the lots drawn, the armor kept, the jokes exchanged at the block) as the corpus's most disciplined death-scene - the constitution's final exam staged as drama.

 The record's saga-structure completes the file: the founding-told-twice (the saga's two halves: the constitution's golden age and the oath)s fatal test at Hjörungavág) read as one argument - the brotherhood)s law proven only by the death that keeps it, the charter-document)s drama-arc documented. And the brotherhood)s legacy completes it: the Jomsviking-name)s afterlife in Scandinavian memory (the professional-warrior ideal quoted by later companies) - the constitution's reach beyond its fortress. The record's treaty-framing completes it: the brotherhood as Scandinavia's mercenary-contract avant la lettre (the oath)s clauses as employment-terms, the spoils-clause as wage-structure) - the warrior-constitution documented as an employment-charter, the corpus)s most modern-sounding institution.

functions: Warrior-constitution file: the band as a contract-state, law before blood
The oath-register: age, kin-feuds, flight, fear, spoils - five clauses
Oath-kept-in-death doctrine: the beach executions as the constitution's final exam
Weather-magic in war: the jarls' sorcery against the raid-fleet

variants.summary: The battle-lay's verse version of the fall.

title.en: Gautrekr's Line: The Founding-Tales of Gautreks saga
title.zh: 高特雷克一門：《高特雷克薩迦》的開基故事

region.zh: 瑞典西約特蘭（高特人的土地）

texts.period: Gautreks saga 14th century (older legendary material); ed. Fornaldar sogur (Rafn 1829); English: Palsson & Edwards 1970

source.work: Gautreks saga; ed. Fornaldar sogur nordrlanda (Rafn 1829); English: Palsson & Edwards, Gautrek's Saga, London 1970

texts.license: Public domain (Rafn 1829); Palsson & Edwards 1970 passages are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: The alternate royal-genealogy file: Gauti's mad northward ride (the king riding his hawk off the cliff-edge - the founding-madness), the cliff-kingdom's law (the elders sent over the rock when the milk ran short - the family's sacrifice-economy), Gautrekr's founding of the Gautar-line, and the frame-tales (Starkadr's youth embedded; Ref the trickster's gift-chain). The record is the alternate-founding file.
summary.zh: 另類王族世系檔案：高蒂的瘋狂北騎（追逐獵鷹衝下懸崖——瘋癲開基）、懸崖王國之法（奶水短缺時以老者獻崖——家族的獻祭經濟）、高特雷克開創高特人一脈，以及框架故事（內嵌斯塔卡德的青年篇章；詭計者雷夫的贈禮鏈）。此記錄是另類開基檔案。

texts.canonical_translation: Palsson & Edwards, Gautrek's Saga, London 1970 (paraphrased); Fornaldar sogur ed. Rafn 1829 (public domain)

narrative.en:
The alternate-founding file holds Gautreks saga's charter-tales (norse-starkadr-gautreks holds the Vikar-chapter). Gauti's madness: the king riding north after his hawk till the cliff-edge - the founding-madness: the kingdom begun by a king lost to the chase, who rode into the unknown. The cliff-kingdom's law: the family-cult of the rock (the elders sent over the cliff when the milk ran short - the sacrifice-law that bought the cows' milk: the household's economy as a cult of the crag, the corpus's blackest founding-institution).

Gautrekr's founding: the son's restoration of the line (the mad king's heir founding the Gautar-dynasty properly - the lineage-record of the West-Gautar kings), and the frame-tales complete the file: Starkadr's youth-tales inside the same Gautar-world, and Ref's gift-economy (the trickster-carpenter whose gifts ascend the chain from king to emperor - the saga's own satire on gift-economics, each gift's profit calculated).

The record's cultural functions are the alternate-genealogy doctrine (the Gautar-line as Sweden's second royal house: the founding told in madness where the Ynglinga told it in migration) and the founding-sacrifice doctrine (the cliff-law as the founding's dark institution: the elders' deaths buying the herd's milk). In the atlas, the record anchors the alternate-founding family: each a tradition's second charter; the Gautar one is distinctive in the madness-frame.

For the database, this node complements the Starkadr-record and the Ynglinga-record: here the alternate charter-file.

The record's genre-completes the doctrine: Gautreks saga's frame-tale structure (the comic-dark founding-tales nested inside the champion's biography) is the fornaldarsaga's anthology-mode - several founding-styles in one document: the madness-charter, the sacrifice-law, the gift-economy satire and the hero-tale, each a different institution's origin told in the same frame. And the saga's reception completes it: the Gautar-line's claim echoed in the Swedish royal genealogies - the alternate charter's reach into the historical dynasties.

 The record's Starkadr-junction completes the file: the champion)s biography embedded in the same saga-frame (the Gautar-world shared), so the alternate-charter document doubles as the great champion)s home-context - the founding-tales and the hero-tale one document. And the saga)s black-humor register completes it: the cliff-law and the madness-ride told without horror - the founding)s institutions narrated in the saga-mode)s deadpan, the corpus)s most ironized charter.

 The record's saga-sequence completes the file: the frame)s nested tales (the madness-charter, the sacrifice-law, the Star-cad youth, Ref)s chain and Gautrekr)s marriage-quest) read in sequence as the fornaldarsaga)s anthology - one document sampling four founding-genres, the corpus)s most composite charter-text. And the Gautar-kingdom)s geography completes it: the West-Gautland sites (the cliff, the farms, the market-ways) carrying the saga)s institutions into the modern landscape - the alternate charter)s geography documented.

Founding-sacrifice doctrine: the cliff-law's elders feeding the rock for milk
Alternate-genealogy doctrine: Sweden's second royal house
The gift-economy satirized: Ref's climbing chain of gifts

title.en: The Jarls' Foundings: Lade, Orkney and the Chieftain-Lines
title.zh: 伯爵們的開基：赫拉迪爾、奧克尼與酋長世系

region.zh: 赫拉迪爾（特隆赫姆）與奧克尼（伯爵根據地）

texts.period: Heimskringla (the Hakonar-jarl material); Orkneyinga saga (13th c.); skaldic jarl-lays

source.work: Snorri, Heimskringla; Orkneyinga saga; English: Laing 1844; Palsson & Edwards, Orkneyinga Saga, 1978

texts.license: Public domain (Laing 1844); Palsson & Edwards 1978 passages are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: The chieftain-lines' founding-file: the Lade-jarls (Hakon Grjotgardsson raised by Harald Fairhair to rule Trondelag - the king-made jarl), the Orkney-jarls (Rognvald receiving the islands from Harald; the vengeance-line: Torf-Einar's peat-cutting nickname - the jarl named by fuel), and the jarl-doctrine: the jarls as the kings' delegated sovereignty, with title-deeds in verse (the Háleygjatal and Ynglingatal composed for jarls). The record is the jarl-file.
summary.zh: 酋長世系的開基檔案：赫拉迪爾伯爵（金髮哈拉爾拔擢哈康統治特倫德拉格——「王所冊封之伯爵」）、奧克尼伯爵（羅格恩瓦爾德受哈拉爾賜島；復仇世系：托爾夫-埃納爾以挖泥炭得綽號——「以燃料命名之伯爵」），以及伯爵教義：伯爵乃國王授權之主權者，其憑證即頌詩（《赫萊吉亞塔爾》與《英格林塔爾》皆為伯爵而作）。此記錄是伯爵檔案。

texts.canonical_translation: Laing 1844 (public domain); Palsson & Edwards, Orkneyinga Saga, London 1978 (paraphrased)

narrative.en:
The jarl-file holds the chieftain-lines' foundings. The Lade-jarls: Hakon Grjotgardsson's grant (Harald Fairhair raising the Hladir-house to rule Trondelag - the king-made jarl as the north's second power), and the jarl-house's poetry-commission (the Háleygjatal composed for Hakon jarl - the earls claiming the same god-descent as the kings: the jarls' charter in the kings' genre).

The Orkney-jarls: Rognvald's grant (the islands received from Harald after the raid - the earldom as the king's compensation), the vengeance-line (Rognvald killed by Harald's son, avenged by Torf-Einar with the blood-eagle - the record norse-ivar-blood-eagle), and the nickname's provenance (Torf-Einar named for the peat-cutting his brothers scorned - the fuel-named jarl: the court's scorn converted into the dynasty's name). The jarl-doctrine completes the file: the jarls as delegated sovereignty (the earldoms as land-grants with title-deeds in verse - the corpus's theory of sub-royal power: power's second story, told in the same mythic grammar).

The record's cultural functions are the delegated-sovereignty doctrine (the jarl as the king's tenant-in-chief: power descending by grant, legitimated by the same genealogies) and the nickname-provenance doctrine (the jarls named by their trade: the secondary aristocracy's self-made names). In the atlas, the record anchors the chieftain-line family: each a tradition's sub-royal power-file; the Norse one is distinctive in the verse title-deeds.

For the database, this node complements the king-records and the blood-eagle-record: here power's second story.

The record's charter-method completes the file: the jarls' genealogies composed by the same skalds who sang for kings (the Háleygjatal's god-descent claimed for an earl's line), so the delegated power's legitimacy is documented in the same mythic grammar as the kings' - power's second story told in the first story's language. And the earldoms' archaeology completes it: the Orkney earls' burial-mounds and the Lade-hall's site - the chieftain-lines' material register alongside the verse title-deeds.

 The record's Hladir-palace register completes the file: the Lade-jarl)s hall as the north)s second court (the feasts at which the Yule-blót's crisis played out - the record norse-yule-blot-hakon's stage), so the jarl-file)s power is documented at the feast-table as well as in the grant - the second court)s rituals attested beside its title-deeds.

 The record's dynastic-continuity completes the file: the Orkney-line)s centuries (the earls running from Torf-Einar to the Norse twilight) documented as the grant)s durability - the charter)s title-deeds outlasting the kings who issued them. And the Hlaðir-palace)s archaeology completes it: the Lade-site)s hall-remains beneath Trondheim - the second court)s material seat documented beside its verse.

functions: Jarl-file: power's second story - delegated sovereignty with verse title-deeds
Delegated-sovereignty doctrine: the earldoms as land-grants legitimated by god-descent
Nickname-provenance: Torf-Einar named for the peat his brothers scorned
The jarls' poetry-commissions: Háleygjatal and Ynglingatal composed for earls

title.en: Norse Founders in Britain: York, Dublin and the Isles' Origin-Tales
title.zh: 不列顛的北歐開創者：約克、都柏林與群島的起源敘事

region.en: York (Jorvik) and Dublin (the Norse west's capitals)
region.zh: 約克（喬維克）與都柏林（西歐北歐之都）

texts.period: The Norse west's founding-traditions (9th-11th c.); sagas and Irish annals; Thing-sites of the Danelaw

source.work: The Norse-west material: the sagas' England-episodes; Irish annals' Norse founding-notices; the Danelaw's place-lore

texts.license: Public domain (annals and sagas in older editions); passages below are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: The British-Isles founding-file: Jorvik's Norse kingdom (the Great Army's conquest and the coinage - the Norse kings of York striking their own names in silver), Dublin's Norse founding (the longphort at the black pool - Dublin's name itself the founding-document: Dubh Linn), the Isles' jarldoms (the Hebrides' and Man's Norse lines), and the hybrid origin-tales (Norse-Irish marriages founding dynasties - the mixed genealogies the sagas preserve). The record is the Norse-west file.
summary.zh: 不列顛群島開基檔案：喬維克的北歐王國（大軍征服與鑄幣——約克諸北歐王以自身之名鑄幣）、都柏林的北歐開基（「黑池畔船堡」——都柏林之名本身就是開基文獻：Dubh Linn）、群島伯國（赫布里底與曼島的北歐世系），以及混合起源敘事（諾斯—愛爾蘭聯姻開創王朝——薩迦保存的混血世系）。此記錄是西歐北歐檔案。

texts.language: Old Norse / Old Icelandic; Old Irish (annals)
texts.canonical_translation: Sagas per standard editions; annals per standard translations; paraphrase

narrative.en:
The Norse-west file holds the British founding-tales. Jorvik's kingdom: the Great Army's conquest (the record norse-ivar-blood-eagle's vengeance-campaign becoming settlement - the invasion that founded the Danelaw), and the mint (the coinage of the Norse kings of York - the founding documented in coin, the corpus's rarest register). Dublin's founding: the longphort at the black pool (the Irish annals' notices of the ship-fort - Dublin's name itself the founding-document: Dubh Linn, the black pool, the harbor-fort's name surviving into the modern city).

The Isles' jarldoms: the Hebrides and Man (the Norse lines of the sea-kingdoms - the hybrid dynasties: Norse-Irish marriages founding the island-lines, the mixed genealogies the sagas preserve). The hybrid origin-tales complete the file: the west's dynasties founded across languages (the Norse jarls with Irish mothers, the Irish kings with Norse forebears - the origin-stories told in both tongues), and the Thing-sites of the Danelaw (the assembly-places of the settlers - the record norse-althing-founding's institution exported). The record's cultural functions are the colonial-founding doctrine (the Norse west's capitals founded by conquest and intermarriage - the origin-stories as treaty-documents) and the hybrid-genealogy doctrine: the dynasties' mixed descent as their charter. In the atlas, the record anchors the colonial-founding family: each a tradition's overseas origin-file; the Norse-west one is distinctive in the coinage.

For the database, this node extends the founding-corpus to the British Isles: the origin-stories of the Danelaw and the sea-kingdoms.

The record's source-criticism completes the file: the annals' notices and the sagas' England-episodes do not always agree (the saga-kings' careers inflated against the annals' spare lines), so the founding-file's method is the cross-check - each charter read against its neighbor's witness, the coinage and the place-names as the arbiters. And the Danelaw's persistence completes it: the law-terms and place-names of the Five Boroughs (the 'gate' suffixes, the Danish wapentakes) surviving into English law - the founding-document's longest echo, written in the modern map.

 The record's coinage-cabinet completes the file: the York pennies bearing the Norse kings' names (the raven-mint's output documented in silver), the founding's hardest evidence - the origin-stories) claims checked against the metal they struck. And the place-name register completes it: the Danelaw's Norse suffixes (the -by, -thorpe, -thwaite names numbering in the thousands) as the settlement)s longest document, the founding-tales) claims readable on the modern map.

 The record's assembly-export completes it: the Danelaw)s thing-sites documented (the courts and wapentakes of the Five Boroughs), the Althing-institution)s overseas branch - the founding-tales) institutions as durable as their dynasties, the Norse-west)s charter running in law as well as coin.

functions: Norse-west file: the British-Isles founding-tales in two languages
Colonial-founding doctrine: conquest and intermarriage as the capitals' charters
Hybrid-genealogy doctrine: Norse-Irish dynasties as the Isles' charter
The coinage-datum: the Norse kings of York striking their own names

title.en: Variants of the Blót: From Household Hearth to High-Feast
title.zh: 布洛特祭的變體：從家灶到高宴

region.en: Farms and temples of Scandinavia (symbolic pin at Gamla Uppsala, Sweden)
region.zh: 斯堪的納維亞的農莊與神廟（象徵性定位於瑞典舊烏普薩拉）

texts.period: Sagas and law-codes 13th-14th c. (older practice); the Grágás and Gulathing-law clauses; Hakonar saga's feast-description

source.work: Hakonar saga goda (the feast-liturgy); Gragas and the Gulathing-law (the blót-clauses); Egils saga and Hrafnkels saga (household-blót episodes)

texts.license: Public domain (Laing 1844); passages below are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: The blót's practice-variants collected: the scale-register (the household blót at the farm's hall - the farmer's rite with ale and horse-flesh; the district-blót at the hof; the national high-feast at Uppsala), the seasonal-register (the three annual feasts: midwinter, spring sigrblót, autumn), the liturgical register (the hammer-sign over horn and cauldron - the hallowing-gesture documented), and the legal register (the law-codes' clauses: feast obligations and fines for absence - the rite as statute). The record is the sacrifice-practice file.
summary.zh: 布洛特祭的實踐變體全集：規模層級（農家大廳的家祭——以麥酒與馬肉行祭；神廟地區祭；烏普薩拉全國高宴）、季節層級（三大年度祭：仲冬祭、春季勝利祭、秋季祭）、儀軌層級（角杯與鍋上的雷錘之印——有據可查的祝聖手勢），以及法律層級（法典條款：祭宴義務與缺席罰款——祭儀即法令）。此記錄是獻祭實踐檔案。

texts.canonical_translation: Laing 1844 (public domain); Grágás ed. Finsen 1852 (public domain); paraphrase

narrative.en:
The sacrifice-practice file holds the blót's variants. The scale-register: the household-blót (the farmer's own rite - the sagas' farm-sacrifices: ale and horse-flesh at the private hall; the record norse-nine-year-blot's national feast at the scale's top), the district-blót at the hof (the goði's feast for the free farmers - the record norse-thorolf-mostarskegg's district-institution), and the legal register: the law-codes' feast-obligations (the fines for absence from the district-blót - the rite as statute: attendance legally required, the corpus's sacrifice-law).

The seasonal-register: the three annual feasts (Snorri's triad: the midwinter blót for crops and peace, the spring sigrblót for victory, and the autumn-blót for the winter's stores - the calendar-of-sacrifice: the year's rhythm as the rite's structure). The liturgical register: the hallowing-gesture (the hammer-sign over horn and cauldron - the Hakon-chapter's documented gesture: the Christian king's cross mistaken for it, the record norse-yule-blot-hakon), the cup-circles by god, and the meat's distribution (the sacrificial flesh boiled in the cauldrons and eaten by the feasters - the sacrifice as a meal: the communion-structure of the blót).

The record's cultural functions are the practice-variant doctrine (the blót's scales and seasons as one institution's registers - the corpus's fullest ritual-practice documentation) and the sacrifice-as-meal doctrine (the god fed and the people fed in one act: the communion-grammar). In the atlas, the record anchors the sacrifice-practice family: each a tradition's rite documented at multiple scales; the Norse one is distinctive in the legal obligation.

For the database, this node complements the temple-records and the feast-records: here the practice-file runs whole.

The record's legal register completes the file: the law-codes' conversion-era clauses (the Gulathing-law's amended blót-clauses outlawing the private sacrifice, the fines transformed into penalties) document the rite's end as statute - the practice-file's arc running from obligation to prohibition, the blót's life documented from household hearth to banned rite. And the liturgical inventory completes the corpus: the hammer-sign, the cup-circles, the meat-boilers and the sprinkling-twigs - the full equipment-list of the north's sacrifice, documented across saga and law.

 The record's scale-economics completes the file: the three registers' costs documented (the farmer)s own beast at the hearth; the goði)s feast shared by the district; the king)s ninefold offering at Uppsala) - the sacrifice)s burden graded by scale, the rite)s social distribution visible in who paid. And the meal)s theology completes it: the gods) share and the people)s share from the same carcass - the communion-structure that made the blót both worship and dinner, documented in the feast-liturgy)s own clauses.

narrative.en:
The sacred-architecture file holds the hof's documented layout. The Kjalnesinga temple's plan (the corpus's fullest hof-description): 'a? - 'temple? - 'with? - 'doors? - 'on? - 'three? - sides? - 'the? - 'the? - - the central hall with the idol-platform raised like an altar, the ring (the oath-arm-ring of twenty ounces) on the platform, the bowl for the sacrifice-blood, and the sprinkling-twigs (the blood asperged over walls, idols and the assembled - the liturgy's equipment documented in architecture).

The pillar-doctrine: the high-seat pillars as the temple's core (the gods carved in the shoulder-wood - the record norse-ingolf-iceland's drift-rite depends on the pillar's sanctity: the temple's own furniture as the settler's compass). The site-choice doctrine completes the file: the hofs sited at landings and thing-steads (temple, market and court as one landscape - the record norse-thorolf-mostarskegg's Thorsnes: the headland's temple, assembly and holy ground as one estate), and the archaeology's corroboration (the Hofstadir excavation's hall-and-bowls structure matching the sagas' descriptions - the hof documented in dirt as well as prose).

The record's cultural functions are the temple-architecture doctrine (the hof as hall-plus-altar: the god housed as a chieftain is housed - the domestic-architecture theory of the temple) and the landscape-institution doctrine (temple, court and market as one estate's offices). In the atlas, the record anchors the sacred-architecture family: each a tradition's temple-form documented; the Norse one is distinctive in the blood-liturgy's equipment.

For the database, this node complements the temple-records (Uppsala, Thorsnes, Hrafnkel's A-dale): here the architecture-file.

The record's archaeology completes the doctrine: the Hofstadir excavation's long hall with its door-alignment and the bear-tooth? - the? - ritual deposits, and the Uppakra temple-complex in Skane (the stratified cult-site with the gold? - - the hof's Scandinavian version), each matching the sagas' descriptions closely enough to confirm the architecture-file's reliability. And the landscape-institution completes it: the hofs sited at landings and courts, so the temple's geography is the settlement's own map - the god's house at the center of the district's business.

 The record's orientation-lore completes the file: the hofs) alignments documented (the doorways and the idol-platform)s placement relative to sun and road), the temple-form)s siting-grammar debated from the excavations - the architecture)s cosmology argued from dirt. And the pillar)s afterlife completes it: the high-seat pillars) carving-tradition continuing in the converted halls (the Christian regalia hung where the gods) images stood) - the temple-form)s persistence inside the church.

 The record's household-temple debate completes it: the scholars) question whether the hof was a dedicated temple or a chieftain)s hall used for cult - the architecture-file)s open reading, the evidence (the long-hall plans with cult-furniture) supporting both, the hof)s nature as the corpus)s own architectural question.

title.en: The Sacrificial Animals: Boar, Horse and Stag in Myth and Rite

summary.en: The sacrificial animals' symbolism-file: the boar (Freyr's Gullinbursti with golden bristles; the Yule-boar's oath-curse 'the? - 'boar? - 'that? - 'carries? - 'the? - 'oath? - - the sonatorrek? - the? - atonement-boar: the oath-animal), the horse (the north's most loaded sacrifice: Adam's horse-heads in the grove; the Hakon-chapter's horse-liver test; the horse-flesh as apostasy's mark in canon law), the stag and the swan (Grimnismal's stag Eikthyrnir and the swan-maidens), and the nine-males doctrine (Adam's clause: nine of every male species - the arithmetic of the altar). The record is the animal-symbolism file.

narrative.en:
The animal-symbolism file holds the sacrificial species' offices. The boar: Freyr's own (Gullinbursti with golden bristles lighting the dark - the record norse-mjolnir-forging's forge-gift; the Yule-boar's oath-curse: the atonement-boar 'on? - 'whose? - 'bristles? - 'the? - 'oaths? - 'were? - sworn? - - the oath-animal documented in the sagas' sonatorrek-clauses), the boar as the fertility-god's beast and the feast's oath-bearer.

The horse: the north's most loaded sacrifice (Adam's horse-heads hanging in the sacred grove - the record norse-uppsala-temple's grove-registry; the Hakon-chapter's horse-liver test: the king's negotiated minimum - the record norse-yule-blot-hakon; and the canon-law clause: horse-flesh as apostasy's mark - the meat that unmade Christians), the horse as the chieftain's burial-companion (the horse-graves of the archaeology) and the taboo's center. The stag and the swan: Grimnismal's stag Eikthyrnir (the antlered source of the world's rivers - the cosmological beast on Valhalla's roof) and the swan-maidens (the valkyries' bird-form - the record norse-helgi-hjalmars' swan-brides).

The nine-males doctrine completes the file: Adam's clause (nine of every male species offered, their bodies in the grove - the altar's arithmetic: male animals and men counted in nines, the number's ritual force). The record's cultural functions are the species-symbolism doctrine (each animal an office: the boar for oaths and plenty, the horse for kingship and taboo, the stag for the cosmos) and the meal-sacrifice doctrine (the animals eaten by the worshippers - the communion-structure the record norse-blot-rites-forms documents). In the atlas, the record anchors the sacrificial-animal family: each a tradition's altar-species with meanings; the Norse one is distinctive in the horse-taboo.

For the database, this node contextualizes the sacrifice-records: here the animals' file.

The record's comparative frame completes the file: the altar-species across traditions (the Chinese oxen of the ancestral rites, the Greek hecatombs, the Aztec? - the frame is species-as-office) - and the Norse one is distinctive in the horse: the animal whose sacrifice the converted law banned first, the taboo's survival documented in the Christian-era penalties on horse-eating. And the meal-doctrine completes the rite: the animals were eaten by the worshippers after the gods' portion - the communion-structure documented in the feast-liturgy, the sacrifice as a shared meal rather than a burnt offering.

 The record's feast-grammar completes the file: the sacrificial meals) shared structure (the gods) portion at the altar, the worshippers) portion in the cauldrons) documented across the Uppsala-grove)s exceptions (the bodies hanging rather than eaten - the grove-sacrifice)s different economy, offering without communion). And the nine's symbolism completes it: the number)s ritual force across the corpus (nine nights on the tree, nine mothers of Heimdall, nine worlds) - the altar)s arithmetic matching the cosmology)s own count.
